Messages.Author: Wilsoros
Messages.Body:
In the spirit of En Passant* and possibly speeding up the game**, I
wonder how folks would feel about first turn 8 transfer then back to 4
subsequent turns. Why? well it gets the game going faster, with less
time worrying about weenies etc.

I know others have suggested these schemes before, has anyone tried
them? Any data to share?

The primary goal I have in mind is help out the larger cap vampires,
get the weenies out of the limelight, a weenie deck could on turn one
put into play 4 two caps, and a fatty deck could only get 1 eight cap,
so perhaps you want to restrict the number of vampires you transfer
to? I would love constructive feedback.

*To those who don't know, Chess was sped up a few centuries ago to
allow pawns to move 2 spaces off the start row and that added the
ability for pawns to skip past other pawns, to fix that situation a
new rule was added, called En passant, meaning when you pass the
opponents pawn they can capture you on their next move.

**You may say the game doesn't need speeding up, fine, your
prerogative, so instead please offer your opinion on this alternate
version.

> I know others have suggested these schemes before, has anyone tried

Oh, sure--there was a whole tournament on JOL that used the Kuta (?)
Transfer rule--you get 5 transfers per turn (I don't remember what
happened on the first turn, however) every turn, but it cost a
transfer to move a minion to your ready region (so it cost 5 transfers
and 4 pool to get out a 4 cap, or more importantly, 2 transfers and 1
pool to get out a 1 cap). This meant weenies were significantly slower
to get out and big vampires were faster. IIRC, it worked fine. There
was also (I think it was called) the Undo Influence format that LSJ
(?) ran a few times at Gen Con or something, where you always had
infinite transfers. I never saw any discussion on the results, but I'm
sure it was played a few times.

> The primary goal I have in mind is help out the larger cap vampires,
> get the weenies out of the limelight, a weenie deck could on turn one
> put into play 4 two caps, and a fatty deck could only get 1 eight cap,
> so perhaps you want to restrict the number of vampires you transfer
> to?  I would love constructive feedback.

I think the idea is certainly solid, but 8 then 4 seems wonky. I kinda
like the Kuta rule better. Seems a lot more elegant, and doesn't just
work on the first turn.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Sep 23, 2:46 am, Zappo <podsv...@gmail.com> wrote:
> what is the reason of this line of thinking? What are you trying to
> fix?

Well, as he, ya know, stated in his initial post, it would be an
attempt to help balance out big vampires vs weenies. This comes up all
the time. And there are plenty of existing variants that people have
tried out along this line that mess with the transfer system.

I don't think it would do anything to actually speed the game up (as
the first 2-3 turns are the short ones; I can't remember a game where
the first 2 turns took longer than 5 minutes in total). But it would
certainly make big minions a little less disdvantaged relative to
weenies. Any number of tweaks (i.e. what Dave suggested, or the Kuta
rule of 5 transfers per turn, but it costs one to move a minion to the
uncontrolled region, or infinite transfers all the time, but your
transfer phase ends if you draw a new minion) accomplish the same
thing. And have been floating around for years.

-Peter

Maybe, maybe not. Yes. Big vampires have a lot of good advantages, but
if you are ousted before you have a minion in play, that doesn't do
you any good. Yes. Extreme example. But illustrates the issue. I want
to get out an 11 cap. You get out 3 one caps on the first turn.
Assuming just stupid 1 cap computer hacking, I'm getting bled for 14
before I have a minion out. Which is a problem.

Yeah, you can play crypt acceleration, but how much of your deck is
spent on this? If it is a lot, you have it reliably, but a big chunk
of your deck is a dead draw after the first couple turns. If you don't
have a lot, you end up not drawing it when you need it. It isn't a
great trade off.

Weenie decks always have a very significant advantage in the early
game, and if they can press that advantage, they do very well compared
to huge vampires. Yeah, a lot of stuff has filtered into the game in
the last few exapnsions that specifically make big vampire decks
stronger and faster, but still, I can see how someone would want to
experiment with adjustments to the transfer rules.

-Peter

That's not the standard rule. The standard rule is decrypting costs 4
transfers and a pool. Since Kuta Transfers increases your standard
number of transfers from 4 to 5, I guess you feel it's necessary to
also increase the transfers to decrypt from 4 to 5 (do you do the same
with Advancing? I don't recall seeing that in the rules), but it
doesn't have to be that way.

> > I feel like weenie decks are hosed pretty good by Kuta transfers
> > already, they need to be able to decrypt, and letting them decrypt and
> > move a vamp into play OR decrypt and transfer a pool in the same
> > influence phase still leaves them weaker than in the standard game of
> > VTES, as well as making a star vamp deck that doesn't get its star
> > vamp a little bit less hosed.
>
> They can't decrypt and transfer a pool under the current rules, either.

Under the current rules, they can transfer 4 pool to bring out 4
vampires in the same turn (by which I mean, "Kuta transfers and the
standard rules are different"). Since you're already limiting a
weenie deck to, generally, a max of 2 vamps per turn into play instead
of the current max of 4, forcing them to also spend longer bringing
out a vamp they decrypt seems unnecessarily harsh.

With regular transfers: decrypt vampire costs "all" transfers (4),
then next turn it costs 1 transfer (2 for a 2 cap) to bring the vamp
into play. With Kuta transfers: decrypt costs "all" transfers (5),
